title: Wagertech <> Jumpr: Weekly Sync

items.topic: Delivery timeline still on track
items.statement: Kobi stated the project is still on track with the delivery timeline and that the solution design is close to build-ready if the client accepts the proposal, provided scope does not expand.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: so far um we're still uh we're still on on track like I I did say like you know once we get through the initial solution design um and we define like what the objects are the field the automations that that is like a big chunk of the work. Um, and uh, if you go through the the the document, not the slides, like it's like we're pretty much build ready from our end if you're good with what's been proposed. / Kobi Kunasekaran: But, um, based on what I've went through so far, I think we're still good with our delivery timeline, um, again, as long as like we don't add too much more other things or um, we don't derail from, uh, from scope, um, we should be good.

items.topic: Open decisions may change scope/timeline
items.statement: Kobi said a couple of big areas still need a decision, and those decisions will determine the final scope and whether there are timeline changes.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, um I think we're still good. Um but there are like two or a couple of big areas that we need to talk through and decide on how we want to move forward because that's going to determine what the ultimate scope and if there's going to be any like timeline changes.

items.topic: Storage and deal inputs pulled into phase
items.statement: Miko stated that two components were pulled in from future phases into the current phase after the deep dive: data storage and the inputs for deals.
items.quote: Miko Sumagang: there are two components that basically were pulled in from future phases to like this phase given uh what came out like during the deep deep dive which is one was like the data um storage and then the other one was basically like the inputs for like like the deals.
items.supersedes_hint: Data storage and deal inputs were originally future-phase items; now pulled into the current phase.

items.topic: Include both pulled-in components or defer data
items.statement: Miko said the decision point is whether to include both pulled-in components or only one; for example, the data storage part could move to a later phase to stay within the estimates.
items.quote: Miko Sumagang: So now like the decision points is going to be do we include like those like two like components? um do we include just like one uh for example because for example like the data part could be moved over for like a a latter phase uh so that like we could like keep ourselves like within like the the estimates that we like provided.

items.topic: Move reps to Platform Plus licenses
items.statement: Kobi proposed keeping a small number of full licenses for build, flow troubleshooting and admin, and switching all reps to Platform Plus licenses, because the new design does not use leads or opportunities.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Now full licenses are still needed uh for people that are configuring flows. Um like if you're doing get uploads and stuff, generally you should be okay with the platform license. Um but we've uh scoped it out to include like five licenses. Like we're going to need at least one for the build. Um, and whether like if you want uh somebody else to be also be able to like build flows, troubleshoot flows, which you're likely going to want, right? Like uh over time, um you're probably going to want at least like one other person, maybe uh maybe two like another admin to be able to go in and uh do troubleshooting, you'll probably want like a couple of uh full licenses. But for everyone else, uh like all the reps, um we should be able to switch them over to platform plus licenses.

items.topic: Lightning Console needed for console mockup
items.statement: Kobi said the base Platform license has a 10-object limit that phase one will exceed and does not include the Lightning Console, which the client's tab/split UI mockup needs; Platform Plus should include it.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Platform is uh bare minimum, but it does have object limits. Um it only comes with like 10 objects which we're already going to go over uh from phase one. / Kobi Kunasekaran: so based off of your like uh UI mockup uh that you shared with like the tab on one side and then the records on the other side and like a tab view that's called lightning console uh within Salesforce and that is not included in the base platform license um but it should be included in the platform plus.

items.statement: Emily and Lina read the licensing info as the console being an extra add-on to Platform Plus; Kobi said it is an add-on only for the regular Platform license, and that the client must confirm final prices with its AE.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: That's how I read it, / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, initially we thought it was an extra add-on, but it's an extra add-on for the regular platform license. But these are things to confirm with a though, like you you're going to want to talk to your AE on the final prices.
items.critic_note: summary_agreement changed from 'not in summary' to 'no': Gemini Details states as fact that Platform Plus includes the Lightning Console; transcript shows the client read it as an extra add-on and Kobi said to confirm with the AE.

And we can talk through like how many integration we / Emily Vandenberg: need. / Kobi Kunasekaran: It should not be a user account like it shouldn't be something that somebody's going to be logging in with and administering the system. items.statement: Miko recommended treating the license change as a future decision, to negotiate with Salesforce a month or two before the next renewal; Emily said that makes sense and later took licensing away to confirm.

But just like note that when you do transfer some like licenses like over they're going to be a lot of the times like basically like they're going to push to have like the same like AR for you guys um to preserve like basically like the the revenue. / Miko Sumagang: and that'll that'll just have to be a conversation that happens like a month or two like before like your next like renewal just to like make sure that everything is like clear coming up to it. / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah, that makes sense. items.topic: No access risk from license downgrade
items.statement: Miko and Kobi said moving users to Platform Plus should not affect access because the new system uses custom objects and not leads or opportunities; moving back to full licenses later (for example for price books or quoting) is not a problem.
items.quote: Miko Sumagang: Everybody else that's going to use like new your new system that we've uh we will agree upon will basically just like use like custom objects. Um, custom objects literally has like no like difference between uh a platform like an actual like license and a platform like user license. / Kobi Kunasekaran: if you're going from the uh full license to platform, we just have to make sure that you're not using any of these objects. And as of now, you are you're not. And I don't foresee us using any of these. Unless you want to start bringing in like price books and quoting within Salesforce, you're probably not going to need any of these things.

items.topic: Lower licenses may reduce included storage
items.statement: Kobi said native Salesforce files consume Salesforce storage, and moving to Platform licenses will probably reduce available storage so the client would pay for extra storage.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: but the native option does cost storage uh so still for storage right now I think you have like something like uh 700 gigs or no 70 gigs I don't remember what the number was that we saw earlier but as you drop down licenses like platform licenses uh you're probably going to like drop down on what's available from a storage perspective there so then you'll have to start paying per terabyte

items.topic: Storage options for proofs
items.statement: Kobi outlined the storage options: keep Dropbox (existing API reuse must be tested), native Salesforce files, Salesforce files plus custom component, or Google Drive/GCP, which he called the most economical long-term option per terabyte.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: right now you have the Dropbox option which which is fine. Um but we'll still need to build uh the like components for the users to interact with it uh from the new like signup object all those things. So there's still some uh work that needs to be done and we can try to reuse the existing like API / Kobi Kunasekaran: I think the long-term option that's going to be the most economical for you guys strictly from a storage perspective is the Google Drive GCP.

items.topic: Proof metadata to automate completeness
items.statement: To automatically determine whether a signup has all required proofs, uploads need metadata (custom object with file URL and category); native notes and attachments cannot be queried for this, so a custom upload interface (for example a screen flow) is needed.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: it'll essentially do the upload save the file URL in that custom object and then we can choose a category uh in that custom object as part of like the upload process. / Kobi Kunasekaran: But when you have that option, then we're able to automate calculating like if uh if the signup has all the proof like the required files uploaded.

items.topic: GCP-side setup done by WagerTech
items.statement: Jumpr assumes WagerTech will configure the GCP side (service account, folders); Jumpr builds the Salesforce side (credentials, API callouts to GCP, upload interface). These GCP tasks are kept out of the Jumpr build scope.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: We're assuming that you're going to do the configuration on the GCP side to like stand up the service account. Um, set up the folders, um, like all of that. Um, but the like setting up the credentials, setting up the API callouts to GCP, setting up the interface for users to upload files, all of that is going to be within Salesforce. / Kobi Kunasekaran: for GCP, these are the things that we can happily help do it for you, but we've kept it out of the uh build hours because you're going to want somebody on your side that has an access to do all of these things.

Um if if there is a case of fraud that isn't somehow it like slips under the rug. Oh, one second. Sorry. / Joyce Kiddell: I agree that we'll we'll want to go back in time like probably to an indefinite period / Joyce Kiddell: But it's not like we need every single proof like queryable like like accessible through Salesforce every single time. You know what I mean?

items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: initially um in your like PRDS you wanted like a multi select pick list so you can have like a deal that's set up to be uh for multiple markets. um multi select pixel list like we talked about before it's not the greatest for uh reporting um because it's essentially like a comma separated value of the different options that are available. Uh the best way to break it down is into like a uh individual object for like the each country and state that a deal uh could be related to. And that's how I've broken it down. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So take a look and let me know if this is overkill or if you're good with just like multi select pick list. Um and the other one that I did bring up from later phases is the deal assignments. So initially in our uh scope we thought we can just get away with uh just a deal object. Um but after going through the discovery and talking with like how the team is associating or doing the assignments and then setting up those links in your agency websites and how those tie back to uh the players and the respective agents. We I think we need to actually bring up the deal rep assignment object as well. So this is a junction between a deal and the rep. Um I didn't scope out any like simplified user interface. So I'm making the assumption that maybe for this phase we go through with whatever Salesforce software is in terms of creating records but we can fine-tune that and like as we start building this you can let me know like if you want a simpler interface for uh for the assignments as well and then we can add that in. Um but what this does is essentially you have your deal uh and then just the same as what your reps are doing now in Air Table where they're assigning a deal uh or like the links to different reps.
items.supersedes_hint: PRD specified multi-select market picklist; Kobi's design proposed related country/state objects.

items.topic: Deal = vertical + market permutation
